title: Risk Factors of the Spread of COVID-19 in Prisoners: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

analysis.scope_and_question: This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to identify and synthesize evidence on risk factors for COVID-19 in incarcerated populations.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar was conducted for English articles until October 2025. Study quality was assessed using the PRISMA checklist and NOS tool. Meta-analysis was performed in Stata 17 using a random-effects model, with odds ratios as the primary effect measure and statistical significance set at P < 0.05.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The total sample size was 176169, consisting of 169117 males and 7,726 females. In most studies, the average age was reported to be around 40 years. Fully vaccinated prisoners were less likely to contract COVID-19 than unvaccinated ones (OR: 0.38; 95% CI: 0.22, 0.67; P = 0.001), while no significant relationships were found regarding sex and age. Our findings confirm that full vaccination significantly protects against COVID-19 in prisons.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Heterogeneity was evaluated via I2 statistics.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Prioritizing vaccination campaigns, along with measures like mask use and hand hygiene, is essential to protect incarcerated individuals and the wider community.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis investigated risk factors for the spread of COVID-19 in incarcerated populations. A comprehensive search of PubMed, Scopus, and Google Scholar was conducted up to October 2025, and study quality was assessed using the PRISMA checklist and NOS tool. Twelve articles were included, with a total sample size of 176,169 individuals, predominantly male. The meta-analysis focused on five studies evaluating sex, age, and vaccination status as risk factors. Results indicated that full vaccination was significantly associated with reduced risk of contracting COVID-19 (OR: 0.38; 95% CI: 0.22, 0.67; P = 0.001), while no significant associations were found for sex or age. The review concluded that vaccination campaigns, alongside mask use and hand hygiene, are critical for preventing the spread of COVID-19 in prisons. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 statistics, highlighting the need for further research to address gaps in understanding.

title: Convalescent Plasma Restores Viral Clearance After Anti-Spike Monoclonal Antibody Failure in Immunocompromised COVID-19 Patients: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Individual Patient Data.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines the efficacy of high-titre COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in restoring viral clearance among immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia following failure of anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapy, focusing on the central question of whether CCP can overcome resistance to mAbs in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A systematic review and individual participant data meta-analysis was conducted, searching electronic databases from January 2020 to January 2026. The protocol was registered at PROSPERO (CRD420251142891). Forty-seven cases (30 from 12 published studies and 17 unpublished cases) were included, with eligibility criteria encompassing immunocompromised patients persistently positive for SARS-CoV-2 after mAb therapy.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: In 70.2% of patients (33/47) with mAb-resistant SARS-CoV-2 infection, SARS-CoV-2 clearance occurred following CCP transfusion, with a mean of 2.7 CCP units administered. analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report the specific SARS-CoV-2 variants involved in the included cases, limiting the ability to assess variant-specific efficacy of CCP. Additionally, the small sample size (n=47) and inclusion of unpublished cases may introduce selection bias, and the lack of a control group precludes definitive causal inference.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize randomized controlled trials to validate the efficacy of CCP in immunocompromised patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 infection post-mAb failure, stratifying by variant type and CCP titre. analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated convalescent plasma (CCP) as a rescue therapy for immunocompromised COVID-19 patients with persistent SARS-CoV-2 viraemia after anti-Spike monoclonal antibody (mAb) failure. Across 47 cases, CCP achieved viral clearance in 70.2% of patients, with higher transfusion volumes associated with improved outcomes. The review highlights CCP as a potential polyclonal alternative to mAbs in resistant infections, though small sample size, unpublished case inclusion, and variant-specific data gaps limit generalizability. Key priorities include randomized trials to confirm efficacy, variant-stratified analyses, and enhanced surveillance to track CCP performance against evolving SARS-CoV-2 variants.

title: Timing, Titre, and Host Determinants of Convalescent Plasma Efficacy in COVID-19: A Systematic Review With Design-Stratified Narrative Synthesis.

analysis.scope_and_question: The efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in COVID-19 has been contested, with large randomized trials producing conflicting results that led to recommendations against routine use.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We performed a systematic review with design-stratified narrative synthesis (PRISMA 2020; SWiM; OSF: https://osf.io/tjcuq) to test whether these conflicting outcomes can be reconciled through three interacting determinants-timing, antibody titre, and host characteristics-using a standardized 91-field extraction matrix applied to each study.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The synthesis indicates that CP is effective, but only under a specific convergence of conditions: when administered early in the disease course, with sufficient antibody titre, to seronegative or immunocompromised hosts who have not yet mounted an endogenous antibody response.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: A second, previously unquantified finding concerns antibody class: characterisation of non-IgG immunoglobulins was nearly absent, with only 2 of 31 studies-both from our group-reporting IgA or IgM data, despite evidence that IgA and IgM are among the most potent neutralising classes against SARS-CoV-2. This hypothesis-generating observation identifies a systematic gap in CP product assessment.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: These findings reframe CP efficacy from a binary question to a conditional one and provide a template for the precision deployment of passive immunotherapy in future pandemics.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review investigates the efficacy of convalescent plasma (CP) in treating COVID-19, focusing on three key determinants: timing of administration, antibody titre, and host characteristics. The review includes 31 studies (20,793 patients; 8 RCTs, 23 observational) and employs a design-stratified narrative synthesis approach. The analysis suggests that CP is effective under specific conditions, such as early administration, high antibody titre, and use in seronegative or immunocompromised individuals. However, the review highlights a significant gap in the characterization of non-IgG immunoglobulins, as only two studies reported IgA or IgM data. The findings emphasize the need for targeted use of CP and suggest a framework for its precision deployment in future pandemics.

title: Inter-hospital ICU-to-ICU transfer of critically ill COVID-19 patients is not associated with increased mortality: a systematic review with exploratory meta-analysis

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review investigates whether inter-hospital ICU-to-ICU transfer of critically ill adult COVID-19 patients is associated with increased mortality or adverse clinical outcomes. title: Allosteric effects of CDR-H3 mutations modulate binding and neutralization of a conserved SARS-CoV-2 RBD-targeting antibody

analysis.research_question_and_background: SARS-CoV-2 antigenic evolution has reduced the efficacy of first-generation monoclonal antibodies, creating a need for antibodies that target conserved regions within the spike receptor-binding domain (RBD). The study aimed to model breadth-oriented antibody engineering by assessing the RBD-directed antibody XG83, which relies heavily on its CDRH3 paratope for binding.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a structure-guided framework combining crystallography, alanine and residue scanning, docking, molecular dynamics, and experimental assays to compare the wild-type antibody XG83 with a modified variant, MuXG83, focusing on CDRH3 interactions with the Omicron BA.1 RBD.
analysis.methods: Crystallography provided the XG83-Wuhan RBD reference structure, while MOE-based alanine and residue scanning identified CDRH3 (A116-Y132) replacements. Docking and 100-ns molecular dynamics assessed stability and interaction energy, and ELISA, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and pseudovirus neutralization measured binding and functional activity against Omicron BA.1.
analysis.main_results: The parental XG83 showed a better docking score (-280.18 vs. -254.2) and greater stability in molecular dynamics, with lower RMSD/RMSF and more favorable interaction energy than MuXG83. ELISA and SPR revealed that XG83 had 40% stronger binding than MuXG83, and pseudovirus neutralization demonstrated that XG83 was significantly more potent against Omicron BA.1.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that non-epitope CDRH3 residues exert allosteric effects on interface stability and conformational dynamics, thereby modulating antibody performance. They highlight that such allosteric tuning is an underappreciated aspect of antibody design, revealing how subtle changes can unexpectedly degrade functional activity despite improving predicted interactions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings inform the engineering of next-generation therapeutic antibodies by demonstrating that allosteric modulation of CDRH3 can enhance resistance to viral evolution. This approach may guide the development of antibodies with broader neutralization capacity against emerging SARS-CoV-2 variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to functional testing against Omicron BA.1, leaving uncertainty about the breadth of effects across other variants. The evidence is moderate, as the conclusions are based on a single variant and rely on computational predictions validated by experimental assays, warranting further validation in broader variant panels.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how allosteric effects of CDRH3 mutations influence the binding and neutralization of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD-targeting antibody XG83 against the Omicron BA.1 variant. Using a structure-guided framework, the authors compared the wild-type antibody with a modified variant, MuXG83, and found that the parental XG83 exhibited superior docking scores, stability, binding affinity, and neutralization potency. The findings reveal that non-epitope CDRH3 residues can exert allosteric control over antibody performance, challenging the assumption that direct epitope contacts alone determine functional outcomes. While the study provides valuable insights into antibody engineering, its conclusions are limited to Omicron BA.1, and broader variant testing is needed to confirm the generalizability of these effects.

title: Critical role of vaccination in preventing severe coronavirus disease 2019: perspectives from clinical outcomes in an Australian kidney transplant recipient cohort

analysis.research_question_and_background: Kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) face disproportionately severe outcomes from COVID-19, and vaccine hesitancy due to concerns about allograft rejection may further increase risk. This study aimed to quantify COVID-19 vaccine uptake, infection outcomes, and rejection risk in KTRs during the Delta and Omicron waves.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cohort study was conducted at a single centre, enrolling all adult KTRs with a functioning allograft as of 22 March 2021. The study period covered the Delta and Omicron (BA.1/BA.2) waves.
analysis.methods: Vaccination status and KTR-related risk factors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models to determine predictors of severe COVID-19 infection (hospitalisation), death, and all infections. Rejection risk following infection or vaccination was also evaluated.
analysis.main_results: Among 986 KTRs, 333 (33.8%) had COVID-19 infections, 79 (23.7%) were severe, and 13 deaths occurred (3.9%). Each additional vaccine dose reduced the risk of severe infection (adjusted hazards ratio 0.5; 95% CI 0.40–0.65; P < 0.001) and death. Older age, lower eGFR, diabetes, and prior allograft rejection predicted severe infection, while male gender predicted all infections. Vaccine type and immunosuppressant doses did not predict outcomes, and neither infections nor vaccinations increased rejection risk.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that higher vaccine uptake significantly reduces severe COVID-19 and mortality in KTRs without increasing rejection risk, addressing concerns about vaccine-induced allograft damage. This provides direct clinical evidence supporting optimal vaccination in this high-risk group.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings support prioritising vaccination in KTRs to prevent severe disease and mortality, while reassuring clinicians and patients about the low risk of rejection. Targeted interventions for immunocompromised patients with compounding risk factors are warranted.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The single-centre design and lack of randomisation limit generalisability and causal inference. However, robust statistical adjustment and clear outcome definitions strengthen the evidence. The study provides moderate-strength evidence for vaccine efficacy in KTRs.

analysis.summary_en: This cohort study of 986 kidney transplant recipients (KTRs) assessed COVID-19 outcomes during the Delta and Omicron waves, focusing on vaccine uptake, severe infection, mortality, and allograft rejection. Vaccination was the strongest modifiable predictor of reduced severe disease and death, with each additional dose halving the risk (adjusted HR 0.5; 95% CI 0.40–0.65; P < 0.001). Older age, diabetes, lower kidney function, and prior rejection also increased severe infection risk, while male gender predicted any infection. Vaccine type and immunosuppressant doses did not influence outcomes, and neither infections nor vaccinations increased rejection risk. The study concludes that KTRs should be optimally vaccinated to prevent severe COVID-19 and can be reassured about rejection risk. Limitations include a single-centre design and observational nature, but robust statistical methods support the findings.

title: Intravenous immunoglobulin recalibrates monocyte responses to abortive SARS-CoV-2 infection across viral variants

analysis.research_question_and_background: Monocytes contribute to inflammation during coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), yet their capacity to support productive infection by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), and the impact of viral evolution on their responses, remain unclear.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we investigated the interaction between primary human monocytes and three SARS-CoV-2 variants representing distinct evolutionary stages (Wuhan, Delta, and Omicron), and evaluated the modulatory effects of intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg).
analysis.methods: All variants efficiently entered monocytes and persisted as intracellular viral RNA and protein, but failed to generate infectious progeny, indicating abortive infection.
analysis.main_results: Omicron infection was associated with enhanced replication-related signatures compared with Wuhan and Delta.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: IVIg did not prevent viral entry or RNA persistence but significantly reduced infection-induced vacuolization and selectively modulated cytokine responses.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These effects occurred independently of neutralizing activity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Together, these findings identify primary human monocytes as targets of abortive yet immunologically active SARS-CoV-2 infection and demonstrate that IVIg modulate monocyte stress and inflammatory responses through Fc-dependent mechanisms rather than direct viral neutralization.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how primary human monocytes interact with different SARS-CoV-2 variants and how intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) affects these interactions. The research highlights that all variants efficiently enter monocytes but fail to produce infectious progeny, indicating abortive infection. Despite this, infected monocytes undergo significant structural changes and activate strong innate immune responses. The study finds that Omicron infection elicits stronger replication-related signatures than Wuhan and Delta variants. IVIg does not block viral entry or RNA persistence but reduces vacuolization and selectively alters cytokine responses. High-dose IVIg enhances TNF-associated responses and reduces IL10 expression, suggesting it recalibrates monocyte inflammatory responses through Fc-dependent mechanisms rather than direct neutralization. These findings provide insights into the role of monocytes in SARS-CoV-2 infection and the potential of IVIg in modulating immune responses. The study's results are based on direct observations of viral interactions and immune responses in human monocytes, with no evidence of neutralizing activity being the primary mechanism of IVIg's effects.

title: Comparative immunogenicity of mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 SARS-CoV-2 bivalent booster vaccines in US nursing home residents.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Nursing home residents remain highly vulnerable to severe outcomes from SARS-CoV-2 infection, yet comparative immunogenicity data for mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 bivalent booster vaccines in this population are limited.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A longitudinal immunologic evaluation was conducted among U.S. nursing home residents who received either the mRNA-1273 or BNT162b2 bivalent vaccine.
analysis.methods: Serum samples were collected 10–30 days post-vaccination, and anti-spike IgG levels were measured using a Luminex bead-based assay while neutralizing titers were assessed via pseudovirus neutralization. Comparative analyses of titer distributions were performed using two-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum tests.
analysis.main_results: Both vaccine groups demonstrated strong humoral responses to the ancestral Wuhan strain and Omicron BA.4/5 subvariants, with spike-binding antibody levels and neutralization titers comparable between mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 recipients.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as evidence that both mRNA vaccines elicit similarly robust humoral immunity in nursing home residents, supporting interchangeable use in booster strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that timely booster administration, rather than product selection, may be the key determinant of protection in this high-risk, immunosenescent population.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s small sample size and lack of randomization limit causal inference and generalizability, warranting a moderate confidence assessment.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated humoral immunogenicity of mRNA-1273 and BNT162b2 bivalent booster vaccines in U.S. nursing home residents, a population at high risk for severe SARS-CoV-2 outcomes. Serum collected 10–30 days post-vaccination showed both vaccines induced strong anti-spike IgG and neutralizing responses against ancestral and Omicron BA.4/5 variants, with no significant differences between products. The authors conclude that either vaccine can be used interchangeably for boosting in this group, emphasizing the importance of timely vaccination over product choice. However, the study’s observational design and limited sample size constrain causal interpretation and broader applicability.

title: Plasma concentrations of nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir required for inhibition of SARS-CoV-2 replication differ between rhesus macaques and humans

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether non-human primate (NHP) infection models can precisely inform optimal dosing of antiviral drugs in humans during the COVID-19 pandemic. It highlighted uncertainty in translating NHP-derived antiviral efficacy to human dosing requirements for SARS-CoV-2.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study applied mathematical models to sequential viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques (RMs) that were either untreated or treated with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir, or both drugs. The models were previously established and validated using SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials.
analysis.methods: Mathematical models were fit to SARS-CoV-2 viral loads from human clinical trials to estimate plasma drug concentrations required to inhibit viral replication by 50% in humans. These models were then applied to viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques to estimate antiviral efficacy and required drug concentrations.
analysis.main_results: Equivalent plasma drug concentrations corresponded to greater antiviral potency in the lungs compared with nasal passages for both nirmatrelvir and molnupiravir. Average nirmatrelvir antiviral efficacy in RMs was estimated at 30% in nasal passages and 46% in the lungs, lower than the 82% efficacy estimated in humans due to a shorter plasma drug half-life.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that dose optimization in humans based on NHP viral load modeling is limited by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles. They concluded that human phase 1 and 2 trial data are better suited for determining optimal dosing.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings caution against directly extrapolating NHP-derived antiviral efficacy to human dosing, emphasizing the need for human trial data to inform drug dosing strategies for SARS-CoV-2. This has implications for the design of preclinical studies and the translation of antiviral efficacy from animal models to clinical practice.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study acknowledges that dose optimization in humans based on NHP modeling is constrained by drug-specific differences in pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and virologic profiles. The evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on modeling and the limited generalizability of NHP data to humans.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated whether non-human primate (NHP) models can accurately inform optimal dosing of antiviral drugs for SARS-CoV-2 in humans. Using mathematical models previously validated with human clinical trial data, the authors analyzed viral load data from SARS-CoV-2 infected rhesus macaques treated with nirmatrelvir/ritonavir, molnupiravir, or both. They found that antiviral efficacy and required drug concentrations differed between NHP and humans, with nirmatrelvir showing lower efficacy in RMs (30–46%) than in humans (82%) due to shorter drug half-life. Molnupiravir efficacy was similar between RMs and humans. The authors concluded that NHP-derived antiviral efficacy cannot be directly translated to human dosing and that human phase 1–2 trial data are essential for dose optimization.

title: The impact of expanded adolescent vaccination against COVID-19 depends on the epidemic status: a mathematical modelling study

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate how the impact of adolescent vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 varies depending on the epidemic status, specifically during the Omicron wave in late 2021 and its endemic phase in 2022.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A mathematical modelling study using the Covasim SARS-CoV-2 model for England assessed the impact of vaccinating 18+ only versus expanding to 12+ adolescents during two different epidemic periods: late 2021 with a large Omicron wave and 2022 when the epidemic was at an endemic stage.
analysis.methods: The study used the Covasim SARS-CoV-2 model to simulate the effects of varying vaccine uptake and onset times, projecting the number of new daily infections, hospitalisations, and deaths under different vaccination strategies.
analysis.main_results: During the BA.1 Omicron wave in late 2021, expanded adolescent vaccination averted 3,000,000 cases across all ages and 1,010,000 infections in the vaccinated cohort within 2-6 months. In 2022, when the Omicron epidemic was at an endemic stage, additional adolescent vaccination did not significantly reduce the overall burden of COVID-19 or within the vaccinated cohort.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the effectiveness of adolescent vaccination depends on the timing and speed of implementation, alongside other interventions and the epidemic status, and emphasized that it should not be considered as a standalone strategy.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that public health strategies for adolescent vaccination should be tailored to the current epidemic status, incidence, and prevalence, ensuring optimal impact during periods of high transmission.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on mathematical modelling, which may not fully capture real-world complexities, and the results are specific to England's context, limiting generalisability. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluates the impact of adolescent vaccination against SARS-CoV-2 during two distinct epidemic phases: the Omicron wave in late 2021 and its endemic stage in 2022. Using the Covasim model, it compares vaccinating 18+ only versus expanding to 12+ adolescents. Results show that expanded vaccination significantly reduced infections during the 2021 wave but had little effect in 2022 when the epidemic was endemic. The authors conclude that adolescent vaccination effectiveness depends on implementation timing and epidemic status, and it should not be used as a standalone strategy. The study highlights the importance of aligning vaccination programs with current epidemic dynamics. However, the findings are based on mathematical models and are specific to England, limiting their generalisability and evidence strength.

title: Health-related quality of life among patients with long COVID according to the presence of a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder: A cross-sectional study.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study examines the association between health-related quality of life (QoL) and a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder (FSD) among patients with long COVID, focusing on the SARS-CoV-2-related condition post-COVID condition (long COVID). The central question is whether FSD diagnosis correlates with impaired physical (PCS) or mental (MCS) component summary scores of QoL in this population.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The evidence is derived from a cross-sectional analysis within the CASPer-COVID program, a multidisciplinary tertiary care initiative for patients with persistent symptoms following COVID-19. QoL was measured using the SF-36 instrument, generating PCS and MCS scores. Multivariable linear regression models adjusted for demographic, clinical, and psychological covariates to assess associations between QoL and FSD diagnosis.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Among 773 patients with long COVID, QoL was markedly impaired, with median PCS and MCS scores of 44 and 39, respectively. No significant association was found between FSD diagnosis and either PCS (β [95% CI]: -1.60 [-3.88, 0.67]) or MCS (β [95% CI]: 1.11 [-1.30, 3.53]) scores after adjustment for confounders.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study did not evaluate the temporal dynamics of QoL changes or the impact of FSD diagnosis over time. Additionally, the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference regarding the relationship between FSD and QoL in long COVID. The sample was drawn from a tertiary care setting, limiting generalizability to broader populations with long COVID.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Future research should prioritize longitudinal studies to clarify the temporal relationship between FSD and QoL in long COVID. Investigations into the mechanisms underlying QoL impairment, particularly the roles of depressive symptoms, physical activity, and pain, are warranted. Clinically, routine screening for depressive and anxiety symptoms, as well as physical activity levels, may help identify patients at higher risk of impaired QoL.

analysis.summary_en: This cross-sectional study within the CASPer-COVID program assessed health-related quality of life (QoL) in 773 patients with long COVID, using SF-36 to derive Physical (PCS) and Mental (MCS) Component Summary scores. QoL was significantly impaired, with median PCS and MCS scores of 44 and 39, respectively. After adjusting for age, gender, comorbidities, hospitalization, symptom duration, depressive and anxiety symptoms, and physical activity, a diagnosis of functional somatic disorder (FSD) was not associated with differences in PCS or MCS scores. Lower QoL scores were linked to higher depressive and anxiety symptoms, reduced physical activity, and pain, while lower PCS scores were also associated with female gender, hospitalization for acute COVID-19, and longer symptom duration. The findings highlight the need for longitudinal research to explore causal pathways and inform targeted interventions for QoL improvement in long COVID.

title: A structural and mechanistic atlas of NTD antibody neutralization and immune escape across SARS-CoV-2 prototype and its (sub-)variants.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the incomplete understanding of how antibodies targeting the N-terminal domain (NTD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein neutralize the virus and how immune escape occurs across variants. It asks whether the epitope organization and neutralization mechanisms of NTD antibodies can be systematically classified and mechanistically explained to inform vaccine and antibody design.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research classifies NTD antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes and profiles 41 antibodies across the SARS-CoV-2 prototype, Delta, and 17 Omicron subvariants. It includes mechanistic studies to dissect neutralization and escape strategies.
analysis.methods: Antibody classes were defined by spatial epitope mapping, and neutralization mechanisms were investigated through structural and functional assays. Escape landscapes were profiled by assessing antibody recognition across variants, including the KP.3.1.1 subvariant.
analysis.main_results: Nine NTD antibody classes (NTD-1 to NTD-9) were identified, including a cryptic epitope (NTD-8). NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies neutralize by inducing S1 shedding, and selected antibodies from NTD-3, NTD-5, and NTD-9 retain activity in Fab form. The KP.3.1.1 subvariant employs dual escape via ∆S31 introducing N30 glycosylation and remodeling the S27-R34 region, undermining NTD-5 and NTD-9 recognition.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The work provides an epitope-resolved escape landscape and reveals three convergent evasion strategies: contact residue disruption, glycan shielding, and conformational remodeling. It introduces a structural and mechanistic framework for designing vaccines and antibodies resilient to antigenic drift.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can guide the development of next-generation vaccines and monoclonal antibodies with improved resilience to SARS-CoV-2 immune escape, particularly against Omicron subvariants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to structural and functional profiling in vitro and does not address in vivo efficacy, clinical outcomes, or population-level immune responses. The strength of evidence is moderate due to the abstract-only scope and lack of direct clinical validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study classifies SARS-CoV-2 N-terminal domain (NTD) antibodies into nine spatially distinct classes and profiles 41 antibodies across prototype, Delta, and 17 Omicron subvariants. Mechanistic analyses reveal that NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies neutralize by inducing S1 shedding, while selected antibodies retain activity in Fab form. The KP.3.1.1 subvariant escapes neutralization via dual mechanisms: introducing N30 glycosylation and remodeling the S27-R34 region, disrupting recognition by NTD-5 and NTD-9 antibodies. The work defines an epitope-resolved escape landscape and identifies three convergent evasion strategies—contact residue disruption, glycan shielding, and conformational remodeling—providing a structural framework for designing vaccines and antibodies resilient to antigenic drift.

title: Seroprevalence convergence masks persistent socioeconomic disparities in SARS-CoV-2 infection risk in Canada

analysis.research_question_and_background: Socioeconomic disparities in COVID-19 outcomes have been documented, but evidence on inequities in SARS-CoV-2 infection risk remains inconsistent. In Canada, apparent convergence in SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence across socioeconomic strata by late 2022 raised uncertainty about whether inequities in infection risk had diminished during the Omicron period.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study analysed serial cross-sectional SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence data from Canadian Blood Services donors collected between April 2021 and April 2023, stratified by area-level material deprivation quintile (Q1 = least deprived; Q5 = most deprived).
analysis.methods: Seroprevalence was measured using anti-nucleocapsid antibody assays. A dynamic seronegative-seropositive model with sero-reversion was fitted to the full seroprevalence time series to estimate quintile-specific forces of infection before and after the emergence of the Omicron variant (January 2022). Models allowing differential Omicron-related amplification by material deprivation were compared using likelihood-based criteria.
analysis.main_results: During the pre-Omicron period, the most deprived quintile (Q5) experienced a 71% higher force of infection than the least deprived (Q1; incidence rate ratio (IRR): 1.71; 95% CI: 1.60–1.83). Following Omicron emergence, the relative increase in force of infection was largest in the least-deprived quintile (48.5-fold) and smallest in the most-deprived quintile (31.8-fold), compressing the relative socioeconomic gradient (Q5 vs Q1 IRR: 1.12; 95% CI: 1.11–1.14). Despite this compression, the most deprived populations continued to experience higher absolute force of infection throughout the Omicron period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the convergence in seroprevalence as masking persistent socioeconomic inequalities in force of infection, attributing this to differential amplification of infection risk during the Omicron period rather than elimination of underlying disparities. This study provides novel evidence that relative seroprevalence convergence can obscure ongoing inequities in absolute infection risk.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings caution against interpreting seroprevalence convergence as evidence of reduced infection risk disparities and highlight the need for targeted surveillance and prevention strategies in socioeconomically deprived populations.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on area-level deprivation measures and donor-based seroprevalence data, which may not fully capture individual-level socioeconomic factors or infection histories. The evidence strength is moderate due to model dependence and potential biases inherent in sero-reversion assumptions and sampling frames.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated whether apparent convergence in SARS-CoV-2 seroprevalence across socioeconomic strata in Canada reflected true equity in infection risk or masked persistent disparities. Using serial cross-sectional seroprevalence data from Canadian Blood Services donors (April 2021–April 2023) stratified by material deprivation quintile, the authors fitted a dynamic seronegative-seropositive model to estimate forces of infection before and after Omicron emergence. Pre-Omicron, the most deprived quintile had a 71% higher force of infection than the least deprived (IRR 1.71; 95% CI 1.60–1.83). During Omicron, relative increases were largest in the least-deprived quintile (48.5-fold) and smallest in the most-deprived (31.8-fold), compressing the relative gradient (IRR 1.12; 95% CI 1.11–1.14), yet absolute risk remained higher in deprived groups. The authors conclude that seroprevalence convergence masked persistent inequities, driven by differential Omicron amplification rather than elimination of disparities. These findings underscore the risk of misinterpreting seroprevalence trends and support targeted public health interventions in socioeconomically vulnerable populations.

title: Healthy vaccinee effect in the evaluation of updated COVID-19 vaccines in elderly populations

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses whether updated COVID-19 vaccines adapted to the Omicron JN.1 lineage provide protection against hospitalization in elderly populations, where unmeasured frailty may bias vaccine effectiveness estimates.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A cohort study was conducted in Sweden among individuals aged 65 years or older (N = 245,696) between October 1, 2024, and March 31, 2025, to evaluate vaccine effectiveness against COVID-19-related hospitalization.
analysis.methods: Vaccine effectiveness was assessed using observational cohorts, with a negative control outcome (all-cause mortality) to detect healthy vaccinee effects, and hazard ratios were calculated to compare outcomes between vaccinated and unvaccinated groups.
analysis.main_results: The vaccine effectiveness was 75% (95% CI 70%–79%) overall, with higher effectiveness in individuals previously vaccinated in 2023–2024 (84%, 95% CI 80%–87%) compared to those without prior vaccination (65%, 95% CI 34%–82%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the findings as evidence of selection effects due to under-provision of health services to frail elderly individuals, highlighting the need to account for the healthy vaccinee effect in observational vaccine effectiveness studies.

analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings highlight the vulnerability of neurosurgical care systems to large-scale health disruptions and emphasize the need for resilient strategies to ensure timely and safer care during future pandemics or health crises.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review and meta-analysis assesses the clinical outcomes of neurosurgical patients during the COVID-19 pandemic compared with pre-pandemic data. The results underscore the need for resilient strategies in neurosurgical care systems to mitigate the impact of future health disruptions.

title: Evaluation of One-Step amplicon-based targeted enrichment for SARS-CoV-2 whole-genome sequencing using the Midnight amplicon scheme.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Genomic surveillance proved invaluable during the COVID-19 pandemic for tracking SARS-CoV-2 variants and guiding outbreak responses, underscoring the ongoing need to reduce whole-genome sequencing (WGS) costs and improve workflow efficiency to ensure accessibility in resource limited settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Here, we evaluated a one-step reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) approach using the Midnight V2 primer scheme for targeted amplification of the SARS-CoV-2 genome, assessed its compatibility with Illumina sequencing, and compared its performance to a well-established two-step method.
analysis.methods: Initially, we determined optimal RT-PCR reaction conditions using the Midnight V2 primer panel for the one-step RT-PCR kit and scaled reaction volumes for both RT-PCR and library preparation.
analysis.main_results: Clinical specimens (n=53) that had undergone routine WGS for surveillance purposes using the established two-step RT-PCR method were compared using the one-step RT-PCR assay.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: For samples with genome completeness greater than 70%, both methods gave comparable results with similar sequence coverage and 100% concordance for lineage assignment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Overall, the results presented here verify the accuracy and reproducibility of one-step targeted amplification and offer an efficient and cost-effective workflow for routine SARS-CoV-2 genomic surveillance.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Analysis of scaled one-step and library reaction volumes revealed significant cost savings for samples undergoing WGS.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated a one-step RT-PCR approach using the Midnight V2 primer scheme for targeted amplification of the SARS-CoV-2 genome, comparing its performance to a two-step method. The research aimed to improve workflow efficiency and reduce whole-genome sequencing costs for genomic surveillance in resource-limited settings. The one-step method demonstrated comparable results to the two-step method for samples with genome completeness over 70%, with similar sequence coverage and 100% concordance for lineage assignment. Additionally, the study found significant cost savings with the one-step method. These findings support the use of one-step targeted amplification as an efficient and cost-effective workflow for routine SARS-CoV-2 genomic surveillance. The study's results are based on clinical specimens and are limited to the comparison of these two methods without extending findings to other related viruses. The evidence is strong, as it is grounded in direct comparisons and quantifiable outcomes.

title: Understanding the interactions and effect of environmental biofilms on SARS- CoV-2 viability on contact surfaces

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the role of multispecies drain biofilms in SARS-CoV-2 infectivity and persistence on contact surfaces used in meat processing plants.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Environmental drain biofilms from pork (n = 12) and beef (n = 22) processing plants were grown with and without SARS-CoV-2 on stainless steel (S.S.), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), tile, and galvanized steel (G.S.) at 7°C for 5 days.
analysis.methods: Biofilm biomass, viral RNA persistence, and viral infectivity were quantified and compared with controls.
analysis.main_results: Surface type significantly influenced viral RNA persistence with PVC, tile, and particularly G.S. supporting increased SARS-CoV-2 RNA persistence relative to virus controls (p 2-fold; p < 0.01) while reducing growth of beef drain biofilms on S.S.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Drain biofilms may act as transient reservoirs for SARS-CoV-2, with viral persistence governed by the combined effects of surface properties, biofilm structure, and microbial origin.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that biofilms on contact surfaces in meat processing plants may influence SARS-CoV-2 persistence, which has implications for understanding viral transmission and improving surface disinfection protocols.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted under controlled laboratory conditions, which may limit its generalizability to real-world environments.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates how multispecies drain biofilms affect SARS-CoV-2 infectivity and persistence on contact surfaces in meat processing plants. Biofilms from pork and beef processing facilities were grown on various materials at 7°C for 5 days with and without SARS-CoV-2. The results showed that surface type significantly influenced viral RNA persistence, with PVC, tile, and galvanized steel showing increased SARS-CoV-2 RNA persistence compared to virus controls (p < 0.01). Additionally, the presence of SARS-CoV-2 reduced the growth of beef drain biofilms on stainless steel. The authors conclude that drain biofilms may act as transient reservoirs for SARS-CoV-2, with persistence influenced by surface properties, biofilm structure, and microbial origin. The study's controlled laboratory setting may limit its real-world applicability, but the evidence is strong due to the direct comparison of biofilm effects on viral persistence.

title: Implementation of an Emergency Medical Service-Integrated Teleconsultation Follow-Up Unit for Home-Based Patients With Suspected COVID-19 During Epidemiological Uncertainty in an Island Territory: Retrospective Descriptive Study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the health and psychological impact of an EMS-based teleconsultation follow-up unit during the first COVID-19 wave, in order to assess its potential as an organizational response strategy for future infectious health emergencies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We conducted a single-center, retrospective, descriptive study including all adult patients monitored by the EMS COVID-19 teleconsultation unit during the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic, between March 10 and May 31, 2020. Among 1255 patients monitored during the study period, 908 met inclusion criteria (mean age 45, SD 17 years; 57.6% female). Most patients (n=724, 79.7%) had no prior medical history.
analysis.methods: Patients were initially triaged through the EMS call center and followed remotely using a standardized daily questionnaire. Follow-up frequency was determined according to clinical presentation. Collected data included sociodemographic characteristics, medical history, symptoms, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) testing status, clinical outcomes (recovery, hospitalization, or death), anxiety levels assessed using a 5-point Likert scale at the beginning and end of follow-up, and satisfaction measured on a 10-point numeric scale.
analysis.main_results: The most frequently reported symptoms were fever (n=177, 19.5%), respiratory difficulties (n=165, 18.2%), cough (n=152, 16.7%), myalgia (n=114, 12.6%), and diarrhea (n=91, 10.0%). Only 10.6% of patients underwent PCR testing due to limited availability during the early epidemic phase, of whom 62.5% tested positive. During follow-up, 68 patients (7.5%) required hospitalization, and 2 (0.2%) died during their hospital stay. The presence of at least 1 pre-existing medical condition and older age were both significantly associated with hospitalization for suspected COVID-19 (P<.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In the context of a novel epidemic with limited diagnostic and therapeutic knowledge, an EMS-integrated teleconsultation follow-up system enabled safe outpatient management while significantly reducing patient anxiety and preserving hospital resources.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This approach may represent a scalable organizational model for maintaining access to care and supporting population reassurance during future infectious disease emergencies in geographically constrained or resource-limited settings such as small island territories.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study.

analysis.summary_en: This study evaluated the implementation of an EMS-integrated teleconsultation follow-up unit for home-based patients with suspected SARS-CoV-2 infection in Martinique during the first wave of the COVID-19 pandemic. The study aimed to assess the health and psychological impact of this system as an organizational response strategy for future infectious health emergencies. A single-center, retrospective, descriptive study was conducted between March 10 and May 31, 2020, involving 908 adult patients. Patients were triaged through the EMS call center and followed remotely using a standardized daily questionnaire. The most common symptoms were fever, respiratory difficulties, cough, myalgia, and diarrhea. Only 10.6% of patients underwent PCR testing, with 62.5% testing positive. During follow-up, 68 patients (7.5%) required hospitalization, and 2 (0.2%) died. The presence of pre-existing medical conditions and older age were significantly associated with hospitalization (P<.001). Anxiety scores decreased significantly from 3.9 to 1.4 (64.1% reduction), and patient satisfaction was high (mean score 8.7). The authors concluded that the teleconsultation system enabled safe outpatient management, reduced patient anxiety, and preserved hospital resources during the early stages of the pandemic. The study provides insights into the potential of such systems for future infectious disease emergencies in resource-limited or geographically constrained settings.

title: SARS-CoV-2 induces robust antiviral innate immunity in PBMCs that is partially mirrored by inactivated virus

analysis.research_question_and_background: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the urgent need to understand SARS-CoV-2 immunogenicity and pathogenesis to guide diagnostics, therapeutics, and vaccines. However, studying live virus requires high-containment facilities, prompting interest in inactivated virus as a safer model.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This in vitro study compared the immune responses of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) exposed to heat-inactivated SARS-CoV-2 versus live SARS-CoV-2. The study used single-cell analysis and transcriptomic profiling to assess innate immune activation.
analysis.methods: PBMCs were exposed to either heat-inactivated or live SARS-CoV-2, followed by single-cell analysis to quantify monocyte activation and cytokine secretion. Transcriptomic profiling was performed several hours post-exposure to evaluate gene enrichment in antiviral and inflammatory pathways.
analysis.main_results: Monocytes were the predominant contributors to inflammatory and antiviral innate immune responses in PBMCs exposed to inactivated virus. PBMCs exposed to live virus showed a more strongly activated monocyte phenotype and secreted significantly higher cytokine levels than those exposed to inactivated virus. Both inactivated and live virus induced similar enrichment of genes associated with antiviral and inflammatory pathways.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that heat-inactivated SARS-CoV-2 triggers fundamental antiviral transcriptional programs in immune cells comparable to live virus, though live virus elicits a more robust cellular activation and cytokine response. This distinction underscores the functional differences in immune activation between inactivated and live virus models.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that inactivated virus may be a useful surrogate for studying core antiviral responses but may underrepresent the full spectrum of immune activation induced by live virus. This has implications for immunological assays and vaccine development, where functional differences must be considered.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its in vitro design, which may not fully capture the complexity of in vivo immune responses. Additionally, the use of heat-inactivated virus may not fully replicate the immunogenicity of live virus, potentially limiting the generalisability of the findings. The evidence is moderate due to these constraints.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the in vitro immune responses of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to heat-inactivated and live SARS-CoV-2 using single-cell and transcriptomic analyses. Monocytes were the primary contributors to antiviral and inflammatory responses in inactivated virus-exposed PBMCs. Live virus exposure induced a more strongly activated monocyte phenotype and higher cytokine secretion than inactivated virus, though both triggered similar enrichment of antiviral and inflammatory genes. The findings highlight that inactivated virus can model core antiviral transcriptional programs but may underrepresent the full immune activation seen with live virus. This distinction is critical for interpreting immunological assays and vaccine development, where functional differences between inactivated and live virus must be accounted for.

title: The Impact of Community Engagement with Vaccine-Hesitant Persons During the COVID-19 Pandemic

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines whether community engagement interventions targeting vaccine-hesitant persons during the COVID-19 pandemic, caused by SARS-CoV-2, improve vaccination uptake, disease outcomes, and trust in public health authorities.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review describes a national panel survey conducted in December 2020, with follow-up in September 2021, where vaccine-hesitant respondents were recruited to participate in three virtual community engagement meetings; 94 of 291 eligible respondents (32%) participated, and multivariate linear and logistic regressions assessed the impact of participation on outcomes.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Community engagement meetings designed to support decision-making rather than solely promote vaccination were associated with nearly double the odds of COVID-19 vaccination (adjusted Odds Ratio: 1.88; 95% CI: 1.06–3.34), about one-third the odds of contracting COVID-19 (aOR: 0.37; 95% CI: 0.14–0.96), and increased trust in the CDC (adjusted Regression Coefficient: 4.16; 95% CI: 0.37–7.94).
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report whether the observed associations are causal or confounded by unmeasured factors such as prior beliefs, access to healthcare, or socioeconomic status.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that similar community engagement meetings could improve public health engagement strategies with vaccine-hesitant populations.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates community engagement interventions aimed at vaccine-hesitant individuals during the COVID-19 pandemic. It reports that participation in three virtual meetings was associated with higher COVID-19 vaccination uptake, reduced odds of contracting COVID-19, and increased trust in the CDC. The review highlights the potential of these interventions to improve health outcomes and public health engagement, though it does not establish causality or address confounding factors.

title: Risk of new-incident mental health diagnoses following SARS-CoV-2 infection amongst children and young adults in Singapore: a retrospective cohort study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the risk of new-incident mental health diagnoses following SARS-CoV-2 infection in children and young adults, as mental health disorders increased post-pandemic but direct attribution to acute infection remained challenging due to the absence of linkage to COVID-19 registries.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using healthcare-claims databases in Singapore, evaluating new-incident mental health disorders in children and young adults aged 6-25 years from January 1st, 2012 to 29th February, 2024.
analysis.methods: Negative binomial regression was used to model the influence of SARS-CoV-2 infection on monthly observed new-incident mental health disorders, accounting for seasonality and overall increasing trends. Separate linkage with the national COVID-19 database enabled the construction of contemporaneous SARS-CoV-2-infected and test-negative cohorts. Cox regression with overlap weights estimated risks of new-incident medically-diagnosed mental health disorders 31-300 days post-infection versus test-negatives.
analysis.main_results: There was no significant increase in risk for any new-incident medically-diagnosed mental health disorders (adjusted-hazards-ratio, aHR = 1.01 [95% CI = 0.90-1.12]) among SARS-CoV-2-infected children/young adults (N = 456,034) versus test-negatives (N = 482,588), except for stress/anxiety disorders (aHR = 1.20 [95% CI = 1.02-1.40]). Infections during the pandemic-containment-phase were associated with a significantly increased risk of stress/anxiety, but not during the pandemic-resiliency-phase when restrictions were lifted.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the increased risk of stress/anxiety disorders among children and young adults post-SARS-CoV-2 infection during the pandemic-containment-phase may be mediated by initial infection severity and concurrent household infection, as indicated by the observed association.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the potential mental health impacts of SARS-CoV-2 infection in children and young adults during specific pandemic phases, which could inform targeted surveillance and interventions for mental health support during public health crises.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on healthcare-claims databases, which may not capture all mental health diagnoses. The evidence is moderate, as the findings are based on observational data and do not establish causality.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cohort study investigated the risk of new-incident mental health diagnoses following SARS-CoV-2 infection in Singaporean children and young adults aged 6-25 years. Using healthcare-claims databases and linkage with the national COVID-19 registry, the study found no significant overall increase in risk for mental health disorders, except for stress/anxiety disorders, which showed a moderate increase during the pandemic-containment-phase. The results suggest that the elevated risk of stress/anxiety may be influenced by initial infection severity and concurrent household infections. The study's findings have implications for understanding the mental health impacts of SARS-CoV-2 during public health restrictions and could guide targeted surveillance and support. However, the study's reliance on observational data limits the strength of its conclusions, and the evidence is considered moderate.

title: Children's social connections, internet usage and mental health during the COVID-19 pandemic in the Global South: evidence from Disrupting Harm.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the cross-sectional associations of digital technology use with mental health indicators during the pandemic in 12 countries in the Global South. analysis.study_design_and_population: The survey included a representative sample of 11,912 internet-using children aged 12-17 in Ethiopia, Kenya, Mozambique, Namibia, Tanzania, Uganda, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam. The study was conducted during the pandemic and focused on children in the Global South.
analysis.methods: We used data from the UNICEF Innocenti Disrupting Harm survey. We modelled the associations of social connection during lockdown and internet use during the pandemic with six different indicators of wellbeing in each country (excluding Tanzania, where there had been no lockdowns) and in the overall sample using robust linear and logistic regression. We controlled for a range of putative socioeconomic and demographic confounders and handled missing data using multiple imputation.
analysis.main_results: We did not find clear evidence for any general associations of social connection or internet use with mental health indicators during lockdown across countries. Rather, our results are complex and demonstrate that the relationship depends heavily on an individual's context; not just on the country they are living in but also on their gender, urbanicity and other factors.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Our results highlight key focus areas for further research.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that the impact of digital technology use on mental health varies based on individual and contextual factors, which could inform targeted interventions and future research directions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report specific limitations of the study. The evidence strength is moderate as the study is cross-sectional and does not establish causality.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the cross-sectional associations of digital technology use with mental health indicators during the COVID-19 pandemic in 12 countries in the Global South. It used data from the UNICEF Innocenti Disrupting Harm survey, which included a representative sample of 11,912 internet-using children aged 12-17. The findings suggest that further research is needed to understand how technology use might act as a risk or protective factor for mental health in young people in the Global South. title: Virus reactivation in acute and long COVID-19.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study investigates the reactivation of chronic viruses during acute and long COVID-19, addressing the gap in understanding the extent, temporal dynamics and immunological impact of viral reactivation in the context of SARS-CoV-2 infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized multi-omic longitudinal data from 1,154 hospitalized patients with COVID-19 enrolled in the Immunophenotyping Assessment in a COVID-19 Cohort (IMPACC) study, focusing on the reactivation of Herpesviridae and Anelloviridae during acute and long COVID-19.
analysis.methods: The researchers analyzed multi-omic data, including immune, transcriptomic and metabolomic profiles, from hospitalized patients with COVID-19 to identify patterns of viral reactivation and its association with disease severity and clinical outcomes.
analysis.main_results: The study found significant reactivation of Herpesviridae and Anelloviridae during acute COVID-19, with distinct temporal dynamics, and demonstrated that reactivation correlates with disease severity, host immune effects and clinical outcomes. It also reported persistence of viral reactivation in convalescence and an association of Anelloviridae with long COVID.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings challenge the assumption that chronic viral reactivation is mainly a result of immunosuppression, showing that it occurs frequently in immunocompetent individuals during severe illness and is linked to increased systemic inflammation.

title: Accounting for methodological variabilities in disease outbreak surveillance using wastewater-based epidemiology: a case study with SARS-CoV-2

analysis.methods: The framework characterised variability introduced during storage, sample processing, and PCR quantification, aiming to improve the sensitivity and interpretation of WBE data through a composite metric (Total Estimated SARS-CoV-2).
analysis.main_results: Sample refrigeration yielded richer epidemiological data than freezing, and CrAssphage was found to have minimal utility as a normalisation biomarker due to its higher variability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study introduced a novel multi-stage framework to characterise variability in WBE methodologies, enhancing the sensitivity and interpretation of SARS-CoV-2 data while reducing non-detects.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more reliable WBE protocols for SARS-CoV-2 surveillance, improving the accuracy of community-level disease monitoring.

analysis.summary_en: This study addresses the variability in wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) for SARS-CoV-2 by proposing an analytical framework that quantifies differences introduced during storage, sample processing, and PCR quantification. These findings can enhance the reliability of WBE for SARS-CoV-2 surveillance, offering a more accurate method for community-level disease monitoring. title: Outcomes of Liver Cirrhosis Patients Hospitalized for Influenza Compared With COVID-19 Between 2020 and 2021 in the United States.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Patients with liver cirrhosis have been reported to experience severe outcomes from both COVID-19 and influenza, but comparative risks between these infections in this population remain insufficiently characterized in the United States.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This retrospective comparative study used the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2021 to identify cirrhosis patients hospitalized for influenza (2016–2019) or COVID-19 (2020–2021) in the United States.
analysis.methods: Baseline characteristics and outcomes were compared between propensity-score matched cohorts of cirrhosis patients with COVID-19 and influenza using the NIS dataset.
analysis.main_results: Among 59,590 cirrhosis patients, 6,800 (11.4%) had influenza and 52,790 (88.6%) had COVID-19; after matching, 6,670 cases were included in each group, with COVID-19 patients showing higher risks of hyponatremia, acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, severe septic shock, mechanical ventilation, cardiac arrest, acute ischemic stroke, acute kidney injury, and all-cause death, but fewer cases of ascites and hepatorenal syndrome.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that cirrhosis patients hospitalized with COVID-19 exhibit distinct complication profiles and higher mortality risk compared to those hospitalized with influenza, highlighting a need for targeted management strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that cirrhosis patients may require enhanced monitoring and preventive measures during COVID-19 surges, and that comparative risk assessment between respiratory viruses in this vulnerable group is essential for clinical decision-making.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The reliance on administrative claims data may introduce coding errors and unmeasured confounding, and the retrospective design limits causal inference; the evidence strength is therefore moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study compared outcomes of liver cirrhosis patients hospitalized for COVID-19 versus influenza in the United States using the National Inpatient Sample (2016–2021). Among 59,590 cirrhosis patients, 11.4% had influenza and 88.6% had COVID-19. After propensity-score matching, COVID-19 patients showed higher risks of severe complications including acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, septic shock, mechanical ventilation, cardiac arrest, acute ischemic stroke, acute kidney injury, and all-cause death, while influenza patients had more ascites and hepatorenal syndrome. The authors conclude that COVID-19 poses a higher mortality risk in this population with distinct complication patterns. The findings underscore the need for targeted surveillance and management strategies for cirrhosis patients during COVID-19 surges.
